name: Patrick Collison
background: Irish entrepreneur from Limerick. Taught himself to code before age 10. Won BT Young Scientist of the Year in 2005. Co-founded Auctomatic with brother John, sold for $5M at age 19. Co-founded Stripe in 2010. Became billionaire in 2016.
notable_milestones_by_26: Sold first company (Auctomatic) for $5M at 19; co-founded Stripe at 22; received $2M investment from Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, Sequoia Capital at 23; Stripe launched publicly at 23

name: John Collison
background: Irish entrepreneur from Limerick, younger brother of Patrick. Self-taught coder. Co-founded Auctomatic, sold at 17 for $5M. Co-founded Stripe at 20. Became world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2016 at age 26.
notable_milestones_by_26: Sold first company at 17 for $5M; co-founded Stripe at 20; became world's youngest self-made billionaire at 26

name: Mark Zuckerberg
background: Born in White Plains, NY. Attended Phillips Exeter Academy. Launched Facebook from Harvard dorm room in Feb 2004. Became world's youngest self-made billionaire at 23 in 2008. Took Facebook public in 2012.
notable_milestones_by_26: Founded Facebook at 19; turned down $1B Yahoo acquisition at 22; became youngest self-made billionaire at 23; Microsoft invested $240M at 23; Facebook reached 500M+ users by 26

name: Dustin Moskovitz
background: Born in Gainesville, FL. Roommate of Mark Zuckerberg at Harvard. Facebook's first CTO and VP of Engineering. Left Facebook in 2008 to co-found Asana with Justin Rosenstein. Youngest self-made billionaire in 2011.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Facebook at 19; became Facebook's CTO; left Facebook to start Asana at 24; youngest self-made billionaire by 26

name: Eduardo Saverin
background: Brazilian-born, raised in Miami. Met Zuckerberg at Harvard. Facebook's first CFO and business manager. Invested $1,000 initially. Relationship with Zuckerberg soured; sued and settled. Now co-founder of B Capital.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Facebook at 22; managed early business operations and funding; graduated Harvard magna cum laude in 2006

name: Chris Hughes
background: Born in Hickory, NC. Attended Phillips Academy Andover. Met Zuckerberg at Harvard. Facebook's spokesperson focusing on user experience. Left Facebook in 2007 to join Obama's presidential campaign. Later bought The New Republic.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Facebook at 20; directed online organizing for Obama's 2008 campaign at 25; graduated Harvard magna cum laude at 23

name: Andrew McCollum
background: Born in California. Met Zuckerberg through CS classes at Harvard. Worked on Wirehog file-sharing program. Left Facebook in 2006/2007, returned to Harvard. Now CEO of Philo.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Facebook at 20; worked on early product development; returned to Harvard and graduated by 24

name: Brian Chesky
background: Born in Niskayuna, NY. Industrial designer by training. Started Airbnb by renting air mattresses in his SF apartment. CEO of Airbnb since founding. Took Airbnb public in 2020.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated RISD; moved to San Francisco; began conceptualizing Airbnb at 26

name: Joe Gebbia
background: Born in Atlanta, GA. Designer and entrepreneur. RISD classmate of Chesky. Came up with the airbed rental idea. Chief Product Officer at Airbnb. Later joined DOGE as Chief Design Officer.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated RISD; worked at Chronicle Books; founded Ecolect; began Airbnb concept at 26

name: Nathan Blecharczyk
background: Born in 1983. Airbnb's first engineer and CTO, now Chief Strategy Officer. Former roommate of Gebbia in San Francisco. Chairman of Airbnb China.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Harvard; became Airbnb's first engineer at 25; built initial platform

name: Travis Kalanick
background: Born in Los Angeles. Co-founded Scour (P2P file sharing) and Red Swoosh (sold to Akamai for $19M). Co-founded Uber with Garrett Camp in 2009. Resigned as CEO in 2017. Now CEO of CloudKitchens.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Scour at 22; sued by entertainment industry at 23; co-founded Red Swoosh at 25

name: Garrett Camp
background: Canadian entrepreneur from Calgary. Co-founded StumbleUpon (sold to eBay in 2007). Came up with Uber concept after difficulty finding taxi in Paris. Founded Expa startup studio in 2014.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded StumbleUpon at 24; sold to eBay at 29

name: Daniel Ek
education: KTH Royal Institute of Technology (dropped out)
background: Swedish entrepreneur from Stockholm. Started web development business at 13, earning $50K/month by 18. Founded Advertigo (sold to TradeDoubler). Co-founded Spotify with Martin Lorentzon in 2006. Launched publicly in 2008.
notable_milestones_by_26: Earned $50K/month from web development at 18; founded and sold Advertigo; co-founded Spotify at 23; launched Spotify publicly at 25

name: Martin Lorentzon
background: Swedish entrepreneur from Småland. Founded TradeDoubler in 1999. Provided €1M seed capital for Spotify. Served as Spotify CEO 2006-2013 and Chairman 2008-2016.
notable_milestones_by_26: Studied at Chalmers; began career at Telia; moved to San Francisco to work at AltaVista

name: Evan Spiegel
background: Born in Los Angeles. Proposed disappearing photo app as Stanford class project. Co-founded Snapchat (originally Picaboo) with Bobby Murphy and Reggie Brown. Youngest billionaire in the world in 2015. Took Snap public in 2017 at age 26.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Snapchat at 21; reached 1M daily users at 22; became world's youngest billionaire at 25; took Snap public as youngest public company CEO at 26

name: Bobby Murphy
background: Born in Berkeley, CA. Filipino-Irish descent. Snapchat's CTO. Met Spiegel through Kappa Sigma fraternity. Built Snapchat's code. Used half his Revel Systems paycheck to cover server costs before VC funding.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 22; co-founded Snapchat at 23; became billionaire at 26

name: Reggie Brown
background: Originally conceived the idea for disappearing photos. Came up with the name 'Picaboo' and the ghost logo. Ousted by Spiegel and Murphy in August 2011. Settled lawsuit for $158M in 2014.
notable_milestones_by_26: Conceived Snapchat idea at 22; came up with name and logo; ousted from company at 22; settled lawsuit for $158M at 25

name: Kevin Systrom
background: Born in Holliston, MA. Worked at Google (Gmail, corporate development) and interned at Odeo (where Jack Dorsey created Twitter). Built Burbn check-in app, pivoted to Instagram. Sold to Facebook for $1B in 2012.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 23; worked at Google; interned at Odeo; began building Burbn at 26

name: Mike Krieger
background: Brazilian-born from São Paulo. Moved to US in 2004. Instagram's CTO. Built most of early engineering and UX. Left Instagram in 2018. Joined Anthropic in 2024 as CTO.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford with MS at 23; co-founded Instagram at 24; sold to Facebook for $1B at 26

name: Jan Koum
background: Ukrainian-born, emigrated to US at 16. Grew up in poverty. Worked at Yahoo for 9 years with Brian Acton. Applied to Facebook and was rejected. Founded WhatsApp in 2009. Sold to Facebook for $19.3B in 2014.
notable_milestones_by_26: Emigrated to US at 16; worked at Ernst & Young; joined Yahoo at 21; self-taught programmer

name: Brian Acton
background: Born in Michigan. Worked at Yahoo for 9 years. Rejected by Facebook and Twitter. Co-founded WhatsApp with Koum. Left WhatsApp in 2017 to co-found Signal Foundation.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 22; worked at Apple and Adobe; joined Yahoo at 23

name: Ben Silbermann
background: Born in Des Moines, IA. Of Chinese and German descent. Parents are ophthalmologists. Worked at Google in online advertising. Left to build iPhone apps. Co-founded Pinterest inspired by childhood love of collecting. Took Pinterest public in 2019.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Yale at 21; worked as consultant in DC; joined Google at 24; left Google to start building apps at 26

name: Evan Sharp
education: University of Chicago (BA, History), Columbia University (Architecture)
background: Born in Philadelphia, raised in York, PA. Parents were park rangers. Former architect. Worked at Facebook as product designer. Co-founded Pinterest as Chief Design Officer. Designed and built Pinterest v1.0.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated University of Chicago at 24; studied architecture at Columbia; worked at Facebook at 26

name: Paul Sciarra
background: Born circa 1981. Met Silbermann at Yale. Co-founded Pinterest. Left in 2012. Later became Executive Chairman of Joby Aviation. Still owns ~5% of Pinterest.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Yale; worked in private equity and at law firm; began working on Pinterest concept at 28

name: Jason Citron
education: Full Sail University (BS, Game Design & Development)
background: Born in San Francisco, grew up in South Florida. Learned QBasic at 13. Founded OpenFeint (mobile gaming network, sold for $104M in 2011). Co-founded Hammer & Chisel, pivoted to Discord in 2015.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Full Sail at 20; started game studio at 23; launched game on iPhone App Store's first day at 24; founded OpenFeint at 25; sold OpenFeint for $104M at 27

name: Stanislav Vishnevskiy
background: Co-founder and CTO of Discord. Met Jason Citron at Gree (acquirer of OpenFeint). Passionate gamer. Built the voice-chat technology that became Discord.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; co-founded Discord after working with Citron at Gree

name: Ivan Zhao
education: University of British Columbia (Cognitive Science & Fine Arts)
background: Born in China, grew up in Canada. Studied cognitive science and fine arts. Worked in product at Inkling before founding Notion. Known for being anti-VC initially. Owns ~30% of Notion. Company valued at $10B in 2021.
notable_milestones_by_26: Studied at UBC; worked at Inkling; began conceptualizing Notion at ~25

name: Simon Last
background: Notion's CTO and co-founder. Worked as software engineer at Space Telescope Science Institute and Nebula Inc. before founding Notion with Ivan Zhao.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated University of Maryland; worked as software engineer; co-founded Notion

name: Dylan Field
background: Born in 1992, grew up in Bay Area. Studied computer science at Brown. Received Thiel Fellowship ($100K) in 2012 to drop out and start Figma. Co-founded with Evan Wallace. Took Figma public in 2025; stock tripled on first day. Adobe deal for $20B fell through in 2023.
notable_milestones_by_26: Organized hackathon at Brown at 19; received Thiel Fellowship at 20; co-founded Figma at 20; spent 4 years building before public release at 24

name: Evan Wallace
background: Studied computer science at Brown, focused on graphics. Teaching assistant for CS courses. Nicknamed 'computer Jesus' (CJ). Figma's CTO. Left Figma in 2021. Former engineer at Microsoft and Pixar.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Brown at 22; co-founded Figma at 22; led technical development of browser-based design platform

name: Melanie Perkins
background: Australian from Perth. Co-founded Fusion Books (yearbook publisher) at 19 with Cliff Obrecht. Pitched Canva to investors for 3 years before launch. Canva valued at $42B in 2025. One of tech's youngest female CEOs.
notable_milestones_by_26: Started Fusion Books at 19; grew it to Australia's largest yearbook publisher; pitched Canva in Silicon Valley at 22; launched Canva at 26

name: Cliff Obrecht
background: Australian entrepreneur from Perth. Co-founded Fusion Books with Melanie Perkins (now wife). Canva's COO. Owns ~18% of Canva.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Fusion Books at ~20; grew it into Australia's largest yearbook publisher; expanded to France and New Zealand

name: Cameron Adams
background: Australian. Former Google designer. Recruited by Perkins and Obrecht as advisor, joined as third co-founder in 2012. Canva's Chief Product Officer. Leads technical development.
notable_milestones_by_26: Worked at Google as designer; founded own startup in Sydney; established himself as web 'rockstar' in the JavaScript community

name: Henrique Dubugras
background: Brazilian from São Paulo. Self-taught coder from age 12. Built Ragnarok game clone at 14. Co-founded Pagar.me (Stripe of Brazil) with Franceschi, sold for tens of millions. Founded Brex at 20. Became billionaire at 25.
notable_milestones_by_26: Taught himself to code at 12; built game at 14; co-founded Pagar.me at 16; sold Pagar.me at 20; co-founded Brex at 20; unicorn at 22; billionaire at 25

name: Pedro Franceschi
background: Brazilian from Rio. Hacked iPhone's Siri to understand Portuguese at 11. Spoke at TEDx. Met Dubugras via Twitter argument at 16. Co-founded Pagar.me. Co-founded Brex. Became billionaire at 25.
notable_milestones_by_26: Hacked iPhone at 11; TEDx speaker; co-founded Pagar.me at 15; sold it at 19; co-founded Brex at 19; unicorn at 21; billionaire at 25

name: Eric Glyman
background: Met co-founder Karim Atiyeh at Harvard. Co-founded Paribus (price tracking app) in 2014, sold to Capital One in 2016. Founded Ramp in 2019. Ramp valued at $32B in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Met Atiyeh at Harvard; co-founded Paribus at 25; went through Y Combinator; sold Paribus to Capital One at 27

name: Karim Atiyeh
education: Harvard University (AB/SM, Electrical Engineering & Computer Science)
background: Met Glyman at Harvard. Co-founded Paribus, sold to Capital One. Ramp's CTO. Company valued at $32B in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Harvard with AB/SM at 22; co-founded Paribus at 25; sold to Capital One at 27

name: Gene Lee
background: Ramp's head of growth engineering. Third co-founder. Longtime friend of Glyman and Atiyeh.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; joined Ramp founding team at 29

name: Palmer Luckey
education: California State University, Long Beach (dropped out)
background: Born in Long Beach, CA. Homeschooled. Attended college at 14. Founded Oculus VR at 19, sold to Facebook for $2B at 21. Co-founded Anduril (defense tech) in 2017. Net worth ~$3.5B.
notable_milestones_by_26: Attended college at 14; experimented with VR at 16; founded Oculus at 19; sold to Facebook for $2B at 21; co-founded Anduril at 25

name: Peter Thiel
education: Stanford University (BA, Philosophy), Stanford Law School (JD)
background: German-born, grew up in US. Co-founded PayPal in 1998 (sold to eBay for $1.5B in 2002). First outside investor in Facebook ($500K for 10.2%). Co-founded Palantir in 2003. Founded Founders Fund. Created Thiel Fellowship.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 22; worked as securities lawyer; worked as derivatives trader at Credit Suisse; founded The Stanford Review at 20

name: Alex Karp
education: Haverford College (BA), Stanford Law School (JD), Goethe University (PhD)
background: Born in NYC. Met Thiel at Stanford Law School. PhD in social theory from Goethe University Frankfurt. Managed investment firm Caedmon Group. Palantir's CEO since founding. Took Palantir public in 2020.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Haverford at ~21; studied at Stanford Law; pursued PhD in Frankfurt

name: Stephen Cohen
background: Born in California. Worked with Thiel at Clarium Capital. Created initial Palantir prototype in 8 weeks. Palantir's President. Interviewed over 4,500 candidates.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Palantir at 21; built initial prototype; became President of Palantir

name: Joe Lonsdale
background: Intern at PayPal, early executive at Clarium Capital. Co-founded Palantir at 21. Left Palantir in 2009. Co-founded Addepar and OpenGov. Managing partner at 8VC ($6B AUM). Founded Cicero Institute.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Palantir at 21; left Palantir at 27; editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review at 20

name: Sam Altman
background: Born in Chicago, grew up in St. Louis. Co-founded Loopt (location-based social app) at 19. President of Y Combinator 2014-2019. Co-founded OpenAI in 2015, became CEO in 2019. Oversaw launch of ChatGPT in 2022. Ousted and reinstated in 2023.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Loopt at 19; went through Y Combinator's first batch; sold Loopt for $43M at 27

name: Greg Brockman
background: Born in Thompson, ND. Joined Stripe in 2010 as one of first engineers. Became Stripe CTO at 25 in 2013. Left Stripe in 2015 to co-found OpenAI. Led recruiting of founding team. Net worth ~$25.5B.
notable_milestones_by_26: Joined Stripe at 23; became Stripe CTO at 25; co-founded OpenAI at 28

name: Ilya Sutskever
background: Soviet-born Israeli-Canadian. Co-created AlexNet with Krizhevsky and Hinton. One of most highly cited computer scientists. OpenAI's Chief Scientist. Led research behind GPT and ChatGPT. Co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc. in 2024 (valued $30B+).
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-created AlexNet at 26; PhD under Geoffrey Hinton; joined Google Brain

name: Dario Amodei
background: Born in San Francisco. PhD in computational neuroscience from Princeton. Former VP of Research at OpenAI. Co-founded Anthropic with sister Daniela in 2021. Company behind Claude AI. Time 100 in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Studied at Caltech; graduated Stanford; began PhD at Princeton; father passed away at 23

name: Daniela Amodei
background: Born in San Francisco. Started career in politics and global health. Joined Stripe in 2013 as early employee. Joined OpenAI in 2018, VP of Safety and Policy. Co-founded Anthropic with brother Dario. Anthropic's President.
notable_milestones_by_26: Worked in politics; managed congressional campaign communications; joined Stripe at 26

name: Alexandr Wang
background: Born in Los Alamos, NM to physicist parents. Math Olympiad qualifier. Worked at Quora and Addepar as a teen. Dropped out of MIT at 19 to co-found Scale AI through Y Combinator. Youngest self-made billionaire at 24 in 2021. Now Chief AI Officer at Meta.
notable_milestones_by_26: USACO finalist at 15; worked at Quora at 17; worked at Addepar at 17; co-founded Scale AI at 19; youngest self-made billionaire at 24

name: Lucy Guo
background: Born in California to Chinese immigrant engineers. Taught herself coding via Neopets. Thiel Fellow. Worked at Facebook, Snapchat (first female designer), and Quora. Co-founded Scale AI with Wang. Fired in 2018. Founded Passes (creator platform). Youngest self-made female billionaire in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Thiel Fellow at 19; co-founded Scale AI at 21; made Forbes 30 Under 30 at 23; fired from Scale at 24; founded Passes at 27

name: Ali Ghodsi
education: KTH Royal Institute of Technology (PhD), Mid Sweden University (MSc, MBA)
background: Iranian-Swedish-American. PhD in distributed computing. Adjunct professor at UC Berkeley. Co-created Apache Spark and Apache Mesos. Co-founded Databricks in 2013, became CEO in 2016. Company valued at $134B in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Completed BSE in Electrical Engineering; completed MSc in Computer Engineering; began PhD studies

name: Ion Stoica
education: Carnegie Mellon University (PhD), Politehnica University of Bucharest (MS)
background: Romanian-American. Professor at UC Berkeley. Co-founded Conviva and Databricks. Original CEO of Databricks (2013-2016), now Executive Chairman. Co-created Apache Spark, Chord, and Apache Mesos. Net worth ~$2.5B.
notable_milestones_by_26: Completed MS in Romania; began career in computer science in communist Romania

name: Benoit Dageville
education: Université de Paris VI (BS, MS, PhD)
background: French-born computer scientist. Spent 16 years at Oracle as architect. Co-founded Snowflake in 2012 with Cruanes. President of Products. Snowflake had largest software IPO in history ($3.9B) in 2020.
notable_milestones_by_26: Completed education in France; began career at Bull Information Systems; joined Oracle

name: Thierry Cruanes
education: Université Pierre et Marie Curie (MS, PhD)
background: French-born. Spent years at Oracle as architect with Dageville. Co-founded Snowflake in 2012. CTO. Left Oracle in mid-40s to start Snowflake because they felt like 'dinosaurs.'
notable_milestones_by_26: Completed education in France; began career in software architecture

name: Marcin Zukowski
background: Third co-founder of Snowflake. Co-created the vectorized query execution engine. Less publicly visible than Dageville and Cruanes. Author of academic papers on database systems.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; academic background in database systems

name: Mitchell Hashimoto
background: Self-taught programmer from age 12. Created Vagrant (open-source tool) while in college. Co-founded HashiCorp with Armon Dadgar in 2012. Company went public in 2021, acquired by IBM in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Self-taught programming at 12; created Vagrant at ~21; co-founded HashiCorp at 23; Forbes 30 Under 30 at 27

name: Armon Dadgar
background: Started college at 16. Met Hashimoto at University of Washington in 2008. Co-founded HashiCorp in 2012. Forbes 30 Under 30 at 25.
notable_milestones_by_26: Started college at 16; met Hashimoto at 17; co-founded HashiCorp at 21; Forbes 30 Under 30 at 25

name: Guillermo Rauch
background: Argentine from Buenos Aires. Started coding at 10. Became MooTools core developer at 16. Moved to San Francisco at 18. Co-founded LearnBoost and Cloudup (sold to Automattic). Founded Vercel (originally ZEIT) in 2015. Creator of Next.js.
notable_milestones_by_26: Started coding at 10; MooTools core developer at 16; moved to SF at 18; co-founded Cloudup at 23; sold Cloudup to Automattic at 26

name: Paul Copplestone
background: From Christchurch, New Zealand. Co-founded ServisHero (marketplace) in 2015. Built Nimbus for Work, hit Firebase limits. Co-founded Supabase with Ant Wilson in 2020. Went through YC S20. Supabase valued at $10B in 2025.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; grew up on farm near Kaikoura, NZ; worked in Australia and Southeast Asia; co-founded ServisHero

name: Ant Wilson
education: Imperial College London (MSc, Software Engineering), University of Leeds (BSc, Computer Science)
background: From Liverpool, UK. Built GeoCities websites in the 90s. Blockchain researcher at Tsinghua University. Co-founded Crypto Squad and STYLINDEX. Met Copplestone through Entrepreneur First in Singapore. Supabase's CTO.
notable_milestones_by_26: Studied at University of Leeds; built early websites; worked on distributed systems

name: Karri Saarinen
background: Finnish designer. Principal designer at Airbnb. First designer at Coinbase. Co-founded Kippt (YC 2012, acquired by Coinbase). Co-founded Linear with Jori Lallo and Tuomas Artman in 2019. Built sync engine from scratch.
notable_milestones_by_26: Co-founded Kippt (YC); co-founded Rails Girls nonprofit; became principal designer at Airbnb

name: Zach Perret
background: Met co-founder William Hockey at Bain & Company. Founded Plaid at 23. Built unified banking API. Visa deal for $5.3B blocked by DOJ in 2021. Plaid serves Robinhood, Coinbase, Venmo.
notable_milestones_by_26: Worked at Bain & Company; co-founded Plaid at 25; built early product and secured seed funding

name: William Hockey
background: Born in San Luis Obispo, CA. Met Perret at Bain. Plaid's first CTO. Stepped down in 2019. Founded Column (chartered bank) in 2022, self-funded.
notable_milestones_by_26: Interned at Bain; co-founded Plaid at 23; built banking API infrastructure; stepped down as CTO at 30

name: Vlad Tenev
background: Bulgarian-born, moved to US at 5. Met Baiju Bhatt at Stanford. Started Celeris (HFT) and Chronos Research before Robinhood. Co-founded Robinhood in 2013. Took public in 2021 at $32B valuation.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 21; MS from UCLA at 24; started Celeris at 23; co-founded Robinhood at 26

name: Baiju Bhatt
background: Indian-American. Son of Gujarati immigrants. Father worked at NASA. Met Tenev at Stanford. Robinhood's co-CEO until 2020, then Chief Creative Officer. Focused on product and design. Apple Design Award winner.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford with BS at ~22; completed MS at 24; started fintech ventures with Tenev

name: Brian Armstrong
education: Rice University (BA, MS, Computer Science & Economics)
background: Born in San Jose, CA. Parents were engineers. Worked at Airbnb as software engineer. Discovered Bitcoin in 2010. Co-founded Coinbase with Fred Ehrsam in 2012. Went through Y Combinator. Took Coinbase public in 2021 at $85B+ market cap.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Rice with BA at 22; completed MS at 23; founded tutoring startup in college; worked in Buenos Aires; worked at Airbnb; discovered Bitcoin at 27

name: Fred Ehrsam
background: Born in Boston. Competitive World of Warcraft player. Worked as FX trader at Goldman Sachs. Met Armstrong through Bitcoin subreddit. Coinbase's first president. Left in 2017. Co-founded Paradigm (crypto VC) in 2018. Now co-founding Nudge (neurotech).
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Duke with distinction at 22; worked at Goldman Sachs; co-founded Coinbase at 24; went through Y Combinator

name: Jesse Powell
background: Born in Sacramento, CA. Founded Lewt (virtual gaming currency for MMORPGs). Helped MtGox after 2011 hack. Founded Kraken in 2011, launched in 2013. Stepped down as CEO in 2022, became Chairman.
notable_milestones_by_26: College dropout; founded Lewt (gaming virtual currency business); involved in virtual goods industry since 2001

name: Changpeng Zhao (CZ)
background: Chinese-Canadian. Born in Jiangsu, China. Moved to Canada at 12. Worked at Bloomberg Tradebook. Founded Bijie Tech. CTO of OKCoin. Founded Binance in 2017, became world's largest crypto exchange in 8 months. Pled guilty to AML violations in 2024, served 4 months. Net worth ~$111B.
notable_milestones_by_26: Moved to Canada at 12; worked at McDonald's; studied at McGill; worked at Bloomberg Tradebook in NYC; founded Fusion Systems in Shanghai

name: Pavel Durov
background: Russian-born. Founded VKontakte (VK) at 21 in 2006, Russia's largest social network. Forced out of VK in 2014. Co-founded Telegram with brother Nikolai in 2013. Self-funded. Now based in Dubai. Detained in France in 2024.
notable_milestones_by_26: Founded VK at 21; VK became Russia's largest social network; built spbgu.ru forum in university; ousted from VK at 29

name: Nikolai Durov
education: Saint Petersburg State University, University of Bonn
background: Russian mathematician and programmer. Elder brother of Pavel. Child prodigy solving cubic equations at 10. Won international math Olympiads. World champion in competitive programming. Created MTProto protocol for Telegram. CTO of Telegram.
notable_milestones_by_26: Won multiple international math Olympiads; world champion in competitive programming; defended dissertation in mathematics at 24; worked at Max Planck Institute

name: Moxie Marlinspike
background: Born as Matthew Rosenfeld in Georgia. Moved to SF at 18. Self-taught hacker and cryptographer. Founded Whisper Systems in 2010 (TextSecure, RedPhone), sold to Twitter in 2011. Created Signal. Co-founded Signal Foundation with Brian Acton in 2018. Stepped down as CEO in 2022.
notable_milestones_by_26: Moved to SF at 18; worked at BEA Systems; found 2600 magazine as preteen; discovered hacking community; worked various tech jobs

name: Tobias Lütke
education: Apprenticeship in computer programming (no university degree)
background: German-Canadian from Koblenz, Germany. Received computer at 6, rewriting game code by 12. Left school at 16 for programming apprenticeship at Siemens. Moved to Canada in 2003. Built Snowdevil (online snowboard shop), pivoted to Shopify. Took public in 2015.
notable_milestones_by_26: Got computer at 6; coding at 12; left school at 16; apprenticeship at Siemens; moved to Canada at 23; built Snowdevil at 24; founded Shopify at 26

name: Jack Dorsey
background: Born in St. Louis. Created taxi dispatch software at 15. Co-founded Twitter in 2006 (sent first tweet March 21, 2006). Co-founded Square with Jim McKelvey in 2009. Took Square public in 2015, renamed to Block in 2021. Also co-founded Bluesky.
notable_milestones_by_26: Created taxi dispatch software at 15; attended two universities; dropped out of NYU; moved to SF; started dispatch company at 24; conceived Twitter idea at NYU

name: Jim McKelvey
education: Washington University in St. Louis (BA Economics, BS Computer Science)
background: Born in St. Louis. Glassblower and serial entrepreneur. Co-founded Square after losing $2,000 art sale because he couldn't accept credit cards. Square's first chairman. Independent director of St. Louis Fed. Founded LaunchCode nonprofit.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated WashU at 22; worked at IBM; published Pascal programming handbook; founded Disconcepts (CD cabinets); became glassblowing instructor

name: Stewart Butterfield
education: University of Victoria (BA, Philosophy), Cambridge University (MPhil, Philosophy)
background: Canadian from Lund, BC. Grew up in log cabin without running water. Changed name from Dharma to Stewart at 12. Co-founded Flickr (sold to Yahoo in 2005). Founded Tiny Speck (game company), pivoted to Slack. Sold Slack to Salesforce for $27.7B in 2021.
notable_milestones_by_26: Grew up on commune; taught himself programming at 7; graduated University of Victoria at 23; completed MPhil at Cambridge at 25

name: Drew Houston
background: Born in Acton, MA. Founded Dropbox after forgetting USB drive at bus station. Co-founded with Arash Ferdowsi from MIT. Went through Y Combinator. Took Dropbox public in 2018. Joined Meta board in 2020.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated MIT at 24; founded SAT prep company in college; co-founded Dropbox at 24; went through Y Combinator at 24

name: Arash Ferdowsi
background: Born in Overland Park, KS. Studied EECS at MIT. Dropped out in last semester to join Dropbox full-time. Dropbox's CTO. Moved company to SF in 2007.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated top of high school class at 18; attended MIT; dropped out to co-found Dropbox at 22; Forbes 30 Under 30 at 25

name: Steve Huffman
background: Born in Michigan, grew up in Virginia. Started programming at 8. Met Ohanian at UVA. Went through Y Combinator's first batch. Programmed Reddit in Lisp. Sold to Condé Nast for $10M at 22. Returned as CEO in 2015.
notable_milestones_by_26: Started programming at 8; graduated UVA at 22; co-founded Reddit at 21; sold Reddit for $10M at 22; co-founded Hipmunk at 27

name: Alexis Ohanian
education: University of Virginia (BS Commerce, BA History)
background: Born in Brooklyn, NY. Armenian-American. Met Huffman at UVA. Walked out of LSAT to start a company instead. Reddit co-founder and former Executive Chairman. Co-founded Initialized Capital. Married to Serena Williams.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated UVA at 22; co-founded Reddit at 22; sold to Condé Nast at 23; Forbes 30 Under 30

name: Adam D'Angelo
education: California Institute of Technology (BS, Computer Science)
background: Born in Redding, CT. Attended Phillips Exeter with Zuckerberg. Developed Synapse Media Player with Zuckerberg. Facebook's first CTO (2006-2008). Co-founded Quora with Charlie Cheever in 2009. Board member of OpenAI and Asana.
notable_milestones_by_26: Silver medal at International Olympiad in Informatics at 18; ACM ICPC World Finalist at 19-20; graduated Caltech at 22; Facebook's first CTO at 22; co-founded Quora at 25

name: Evan Williams
background: Born in Clarks, NE. Grew up on a farm. Co-founded Pyra Labs (Blogger, coined 'blogger') in 1999, sold to Google in 2003. Co-founded Twitter in 2006, CEO 2008-2010. Founded Medium in 2012. Co-founded Obvious Ventures in 2014.
notable_milestones_by_26: Dropped out of University of Nebraska; worked various jobs; started playing with internet in 1993; moved to Silicon Valley in 1997 at 25

name: Chris Best
background: Co-founder and CEO of Substack. Previously co-founder and CTO of Kik Messenger. Inspired by Ben Thompson's Stratechery newsletter model. Went through YC W18.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; co-founded Kik Messenger; served as CTO before founding Substack

name: Hamish McKenzie
background: Co-founder and COO of Substack. Former tech reporter at PandoDaily. Former editorial adviser at Kik. Inspired by Stratechery subscription model. Went through YC W18.
notable_milestones_by_26: Information limited; worked as tech journalist; editorial adviser at Kik before co-founding Substack

name: Tom Preston-Werner
background: Born in Dubuque, IA. Created Gravatar (sold to Automattic in 2007). Created Jekyll, TOML, SemVer. Co-founded GitHub in 2008. Resigned as CEO in 2014 after harassment investigation. Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5B in 2018.
notable_milestones_by_26: Dropped out of Harvey Mudd at 20; created Gravatar; sold Gravatar to Automattic at 28; co-founded GitHub at 29

name: Chris Wanstrath
background: Born in Ohio. Self-taught programmer. Worked at CNET on GameSpot and Chowhound. Ran Ruby on Rails consulting shop with PJ Hyett. Co-founded GitHub in 2008. CEO 2012-2014 and 2014-2018. Created Atom editor, Resque, Mustache.
notable_milestones_by_26: Self-taught programmer; dropped out of University of Cincinnati; worked at CNET; co-founded GitHub at 23; 100K users by 24

name: PJ Hyett
background: Born in Naperville, IL. Senior software engineer at CNET. Co-founded GitHub with Wanstrath and Preston-Werner. Also a racing driver (FIA Bronze).
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated North Central College; worked at CNET; ran Rails consulting with Wanstrath; co-founded GitHub at 25

name: Scott Chacon
education: UC San Diego (BA, Computing in the Arts)
background: Started as theater major at UC San Diego. Git evangelist and author of 'Pro Git.' GitHub's fourth co-founder and CIO. Helped grow GitHub from 4 founders to 450 employees. Later co-founded Chatterbug and GitButler. Based in Berlin.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated UCSD at 22; became Git expert; wrote Pro Git; co-founded GitHub at 28

name: Sid Sijbrandij
background: Dutch from Netherlands. Built recreational submarines at U-Boat Worx for 4 years. Worked at Dutch Ministry of Justice. Taught himself Ruby in 2007. Commercialized GitLab in 2012. Went through YC W15. Took GitLab public in 2021 at $15B valuation. All-remote company pioneer.
notable_milestones_by_26: Studied applied physics then management science; graduated at 25; built submarines; taught himself programming at 29

name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
background: Ukrainian from Kharkiv. Created GitLab in 2011 as open source tool. Co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sijbrandij in 2013. Forbes 30 Under 30. Ranked 28th in Forbes' 100 richest Ukrainians.
notable_milestones_by_26: Created GitLab at 22; co-founded GitLab Inc. at 24; Forbes 30 Under 30; company became unicorn at 29

name: Mike Cannon-Brookes
education: University of New South Wales (BS, Information Systems)
background: Australian-American. Born in Connecticut, grew up in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Australia. Co-founded Atlassian with Scott Farquhar in 2002, funded with credit cards. Bootstrapped for years. Took public in 2015 at $4.37B. Australia's first tech billionaires.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated UNSW at 23; co-founded Atlassian at 23; bootstrapped with $10K credit card debt; built to profitability

name: Scott Farquhar
education: University of New South Wales (BS, Information Technology)
background: Australian from Parramatta, Sydney. Attended James Ruse Agricultural High School. Met Cannon-Brookes at UNSW. Co-founded Atlassian to earn graduate salary without working for someone else. 'Accidental billionaire.' Australia's first tech billionaire.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated UNSW at 23; co-founded Atlassian at 23; bootstrapped with credit cards; built to profitability

name: Emmett Shear
background: Grew up in Seattle. Met Justin Kan at age 8 at gifted school. Co-founded Justin.tv in 2007 with Kan, Seibel, and Vogt. Became Twitch CEO when it spun off. Sold to Amazon for $970M in 2014. YC partner 2011. Briefly interim CEO of OpenAI in 2023.
notable_milestones_by_26: Met Kan at 8; attended gifted school; graduated Yale at 22; co-founded Justin.tv at 24; launched Twitch at 28

name: Justin Kan
background: Born in Seattle. Met Shear at age 8. Co-founded Justin.tv (lifecasting with webcam on head) in 2007. Co-founded Socialcam (sold to Autodesk for $60M). Co-founded Atrium (legal tech, shut down 2020). Launched NFT marketplace Fractal in 2021.
notable_milestones_by_26: Met Shear at 8; graduated Yale at 22; co-founded Justin.tv at 23; popularized 'lifecasting'; sold Socialcam at 29

name: Michael Seibel
background: Born in Brooklyn, NY. Met Kan at Yale. Justin.tv's CEO (2007-2011). Co-founded Socialcam (sold for $60M). YC partner, led accelerator 2016-2024. Board member of Reddit, Dropbox, Kalshi. One of most influential Black investors in Silicon Valley.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Yale at 23; finance director for US Senate campaign at 24; co-founded Justin.tv at 25; CEO of Justin.tv at 25

name: Kyle Vogt
background: Born in Kansas City, KS. Interested in autonomous driving from young age. Participated in 2004 DARPA Grand Challenge. Co-founded Justin.tv/Twitch (built streaming tech). Co-founded Socialcam (sold for $60M). Founded Cruise Automation in 2013, sold to GM for $1B+. Cruise reached $30B valuation.
notable_milestones_by_26: Participated in DARPA Grand Challenge at 20; interned at iRobot; competed in BattleBots; co-founded Justin.tv at 23; left MIT junior year

name: Max Levchin
education: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (BS, Computer Science)
background: Ukrainian-born, moved to US in 1991 as Jewish refugee with $700. Co-founded PayPal (as Confinity) with Thiel in 1998. PayPal's CTO. Sold to eBay for $1.5B in 2002. Founded Slide (sold to Google for $179M). Founded Affirm (BNPL) in 2012, took public in 2021. Key member of PayPal Mafia.
notable_milestones_by_26: Emigrated to US at 16; graduated UIUC at 22; co-founded 4 startups in college; co-founded PayPal at 23; created CAPTCHA technology

name: Biz Stone
education: Northeastern University (attended), UMass Boston (attended) - no degree
background: Born in Boston. Attended but did not graduate from Northeastern and UMass Boston. Creative director at Xanga (1999-2001). Co-founded Twitter with Dorsey and Williams in 2006. Left Twitter in 2011. Co-founded Jelly (sold to Pinterest in 2017).
notable_milestones_by_26: Dropped out of two universities; worked at Little Brown publishing; discovered internet; worked at Xanga

name: Caterina Fake
background: Born in Pittsburgh. Graduated Vassar in 1991. Worked at Netscape, Salon.com. Co-founded Ludicorp with Stewart Butterfield in 2002. Launched Flickr in 2004, sold to Yahoo in 2005. Co-founded Hunch in 2007. Time 100 in 2006. Chairwoman of Etsy.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Vassar at 22; worked as painter's assistant, investment banker, dive shop; taught herself web design; worked at Netscape at 28

name: Justin Rosenstein
background: Born in Bay Area. Attended College Preparatory School in Oakland. Graduated Stanford at 20 with math degree. Mayfield Fellows Program. Product Manager at Google (2004-2007). Engineering Manager at Facebook (2007-2008). Co-founded Asana with Moskovitz. Took public in 2020.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated Stanford at 20; worked at Google for 3 years; joined Facebook at 24; co-founded Asana at 25

name: Matt Huang
background: Father was MIT economics professor and LTCM managing director. Founded Hotspots (YC company, acquired by Twitter in 2012). Partner at Sequoia Capital. Co-founded Paradigm (crypto VC) with Fred Ehrsam in 2018. Early investor in ByteDance, Instacart, Benchling. Serves on Stripe board.
notable_milestones_by_26: Graduated MIT at 22; founded Hotspots; sold to Twitter at 24; joined Sequoia Capital; purchased first Bitcoin from MtGox at 24
